title: On a theorem of M. Jodeit Jr. on pushforwards of Fourier multipliers
summary: A classical theorem of M. Jodeit Jr. implies that if a compactly supported distribution on $\mathbf{R}^d$ is the symbol of an $L^p(\mathbf{R}^d)$-$L^q(\mathbf{R}^d)$ Fourier multiplier, then its pushforward by the canonical homomorphism from $\mathbf{R}^d$ to $\mathbf{T}^d$ is the symbol of an $\ell^p(\mathbf{Z}^d)$-$\ell^q(\mathbf{Z}^d)$ Fourier multiplier.
